title: fix(cli): objectui check prints the refused key and path, and never calls an unvalidated file passed (objectui#11007)
body:
Fixes #11007

Clause-②: no

`domain:ui` seat 2, branch `claude/issue-11007-check-prints-key`, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`. Placeholders are spelled in capitals (`FILE`) because GitHub strips tag-shaped text from a body.

## What this changes

`objectui check` recognises a JSON file in one of two ways: a structural root key (`children`, `className`, …) admits it without parsing it, or the whole document validates. Measured on `origin/main` at `bf7ab35ce` before this change, with the card's two documents:

- A root `object-map` whose `map` block carries `latitudeFieId` was listed under "did not validate" as `map.json (type "object-map")`. The validator's issue was already in hand from the recognising parse, and was dropped.
- The same node under a page's `children` was admitted on `children` and never parsed. The run ended `✓ All checks passed`. No exit call in either run.

Per the triage ruling (both halves, narrowly):

- **(a)** Each "did not validate" entry now carries one indented line: the first issue's path, spelled by the formatter behind `objectui validate`'s `Path:` line, and its message, with the issue count when there is more than one. For the card's root case it reads `Issue at map: Unrecognized key: "latitudeFieId"`. It reuses the issues of the parse the recogniser already ran. Skipped (foreign) files still get no diagnosis.
- **(b)** The no-error close is a tally: `ObjectUI schema files: V validated, S recognised but not validated, U did not validate. This sweep is advisory; run objectui validate FILE for a verdict.` Nothing reads as a pass. The parse-error close (`Found N errors`, exit 1) is untouched.
- No nested walk in `check`. A structurally admitted file is still not parsed, and a pin holds that boundary: a later walk turns it red.
- Exit codes do not move.

## Surface beyond the claim's file list, and why

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/issue-path.ts` (new, `formatIssuePath`), and `validate.ts` switched to it.** The suggested route said to reuse `validate`'s formatter rather than copy it. It was an inline ternary with no export, so it moved into one helper that both commands call. `validate`'s output is byte-identical: same expression, and its three suites are green below.
- **A comment in `validate.ts` and the header of `utils/union-arm-diagnostics.ts`** each said `validate` is "the repository's only zod-issue printer". This change makes that false, so both now say what `check` prints (one first-issue line, no arm selection).
- **Three pending changesets get an appended dated note.** Their existing text and declarations are unchanged. Each would otherwise publish a sentence this change makes false, in the same release: `7004-cli-union-arm-selection.md` (`check` "has no zod-issue printer"), `7694-chart-series-chart-type-alias-refusal.md` ("without the issue") and `6475-gantt-block-face-declared.md` ("without naming the missing field"). The shape follows the 2026-09-25 dated notes (objectui#10524) on the same files. `check-changeset-overwrite` reports the three as modified, with declarations unchanged (report-only).

**Closing text pinned next to an exit code.** The order asked for this to be reported, not acted on. Four existing tests asserted `All checks passed` beside their exit-code assertion: `check-jsonc-parse` (two), `check-schema-marker` and `check-validity-recogniser`. `check-known-types` used the same line as its "not a failure" signal. Each text assertion now reads the tally through `closingLine(...)`. Every exit-code assertion is unchanged.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/__tests__/check-first-issue-11007.test.ts`, 8 tests:

- The root typo prints the refused key and the path `map`.
- A two-segment first-issue path prints as `map → zoom`.
- The issue count appears when there is more than one issue.
- There is still one entry per file.
- The nested typo is not reported as passed: no printed line matches `/pass/i`, the tally is 0 / 1 / 0, and there is no exit call.
- Each bucket is counted apart.
- The parse-error close is unchanged.
- There is no nested walk: a broken page and a clean page are counted the same, while `safeValidateSchema` tells them apart.

Expected text comes from `describeFirstIssue` and `closingLine`, fed with real `safeValidateSchema` issues. The assertions pin the subject (key, path, counts), not the wording.

**Ablations.** Each was one-shot, run on the committed tree at `762723318` through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each restore was proven: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. No permanent test was added.

- **i. Drop the first-issue print:** 4 failed, 48 passed. The four first-issue pins failed.
- **ii. Put the old pass line back at the call site:** 8 failed, 44 passed, across all five files. That is the five updated sibling assertions plus the three new close pins. The first attempt was a no-op: the tool refused before running because the replacement contained its anchor. It was rerun with a different anchor.
- **iii. Parse structurally admitted files (a nested walk):** 1 failed, 51 passed. Only the no-walk pin failed.

## Gates, all at `762723318` (the final commit)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/cli/` → `Test Files 22 passed (22)`, `Tests 302 passed (302)`. The base has 21 files.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` → exit 0. That is the only workspace package the CLI's source imports (`@object-ui/types/zod`); the other `@object-ui/*` hits are template strings.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli type-check` (`tsc --noEmit`) → exit 0. `--listFiles` includes the new test, `issue-path.ts` and `check.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli build`, then `pnpm check` (the repo-tree run `lint.yml` makes) → exit 0. Output is below.
- eslint, run the way the package `lint` script runs it (`eslint src` in `packages/cli`, inline config honoured): 48 files, 0 errors, 5 warnings. All five are `no-explicit-any` in untouched files. `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions`, no type-checked preset), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- Changeset and byte gates: `check-changeset-presence` ✅ (1 added), `check-changeset-no-major` ✅, `check-control-bytes` ✅, `check-new-line-citations` 0 new, `check-pending-changeset-literals` ✅.
- `check-changeset-claims` is report-only. It names two pending changesets that mention touched files: 6320 (the ignore list in `check.ts`) and 7658 (headings in `cli.mdx`). Both still hold.
- Other gates: `check-test-path-roots` ✅, `check-unreferenced-sources` ✅, `check-doc-fences` ✅, `check-doc-types` ✅, `check-spec-symbols` ✅, `check-doc-example-ids` ✅, `check-doc-example-readers` ✅, `check-doc-links` ✅.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-examples` and `check:doc-snippets`. Their prerequisite is not met: they need a scoped build of 34 packages. This diff adds no TypeScript block to any document; its one new fence is `text`. CI runs both.

`pnpm check` on this tree (`FILE` stands for the placeholder the command prints):

```text
Object UI Schema Check
Analyzing 633 files...
⚠️ 1 file carries a registered ObjectUI component type but did not validate as an ObjectUI schema:
   packages/vscode-extension/schemas/objectui-schema.json (type "object")
     Issue at type: Invalid input
   Run `objectui validate FILE` on any of them for the full diagnosis.
   Either the document is off-spec, or its component type is not modelled by @object-ui/types.
   These are NOT counted as skipped: a schema that fails validation is a broken schema, not a foreign file.
Skipped 46 files with a root "type" that no ObjectUI recogniser admitted.
  A file is checked when its root carries an ObjectUI structural key: body, children, className, style, placeholder, visible, visibleWhen, visibleOn, hidden, hiddenOn, disabled, disabledOn, testId, ariaLabel.
  It is also checked when the whole document validates as an ObjectUI component schema.
ObjectUI schema files: 265 validated, 167 recognised but not validated, 1 did not validate. This sweep is advisory; run `objectui validate FILE` for a verdict.
```

## Acceptance notes

None of these was filed.

- **A document whose `type` selects no arm gets the bare message.** Its first issue is the discriminator's `Issue at type: Invalid input`. The only hit on this tree is `packages/vscode-extension/schemas/objectui-schema.json`, a JSON Schema document with `"type": "object"`, which is the bucket's known false positive. `objectui validate` adds its "No arm accepts type" note from arm selection, which the ruling keeps out of `check`. This is polish.
- **`content/docs/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx` says `check` "passes" a structurally admitted chatbot document.** It still exits 0 but no longer prints a pass line. Left as is.
- **YAML files are counted but never read.** They appear in `Analyzing N files...`, as before and as the source already states. The tally counts JSON only.
